c_deg.data_reference: kenniston2003linkage; ATP per amino acid for ATP-dependent proteolysis: ClpXP hydrolyses about 1 ATP per residue it translocates, plus 10 to over 500 ATP per substrate to unfold it, more for more stable proteins (Kenniston et al. 2003; single-molecule steps of 5-8 residues per power stroke, Maillard et al. 2011, put translocation nearer 0.2-0.5); 1 taken (confidence: medium, the unfolding share varies with the protein)

c_recycle.data_reference: lynch2015bioenergetic; 0.25-1 ATP per amino acid recycled (Lynch & Marinov 2015 supplement)

k_deg.data_reference: maurizi1992proteases; bulk degradation of the stable protein in growing E. coli about 1%/h (Maurizi 1992 after Pine 1970; BioNumbers BNID 109924); 0.6%/h in Willetts 1967 (growing cells); most proteins are stable and leave growing cells by dilution (Gupta et al. 2024). Rises to about 5%/h in carbon, nitrogen or phosphate starvation (Willetts 1967, non-growing cells), not modelled (confidence: high)

C_ATP.data_reference: bennett2009absolute; glucose-fed, exponentially growing E. coli: ATP 9.6 mM

C_G6P.data_reference: chassagnole2002dynamic; glucose 6-phosphate in the resting cell, a chosen operating point in the measured range: E. coli in glucose-limited chemostat culture (D = 0.1 /h) 3.48 mM G6P (Chassagnole et al. 2002, Table V; the initial value of their model, BioModels BIOMD0000000051), exponentially growing on glucose 8.8 mM hexose phosphates (G6P + F6P + G1P; Bennett et al. 2009, Table 1, which does not resolve G6P). 1 mM, below the growing cells' values, as the level-1 cell runs at its maintenance flux (confidence: medium; the range 0.5-4 mM is well supported, the exact resting value is a choice)

C_glc.data_reference: unreferenced_placeholder; design value; no measurement found (searched 2026-10-23): free glucose inside the cell (no E. coli measurement: PTS uptake delivers G6P). glucose inside an uptake-limited cell at rest: low, so glycolysis has ~50x headroom (growing fermenters run 10-40x their maintenance flux)

H_i.data_reference: derived: free H+ = 10^-pH_i M (pH_i: slonczewski1981ph, sourced)

n_reg.data_reference: definitional; steepness n of the hardcoded regulation function f = 1/(1 + u^n) of the shortfall u below rest (u = 1 half-way) by which a falling metabolite lowers an expression, growth or maintenance target (designer 2026-10-12: hardcoded for now, experts will choose the function); a steep, switch-like fall, as the stringent response (ppGpp) cuts ribosome and protein synthesis sharply on energy or carbon downshift (Potrykus & Cashel 2008; confidence: medium for the qualitative behaviour, the value itself is a design choice). n > 1 keeps f smooth at rest (C^3 for n = 4)
